comments.content: Clamping each width to ≥1px avoids zero/negative columns, but when `total <= 0` the row becomes `columns` px of cells + `(columns-1) * spacing`, which can exceed `availableSize` (up to 16px + 15 spacings) — the row overflows the grid's constraints and the trailing cards are clipped. It needs a degenerate pairing to fire (huge `contentPaddingHorizontal` vs. a narrow measured width, or a huge px `spacing`); I verified the five current call sites (12.dp/0.dp padding, 10.dp spacing) cannot reach it. Still, the comment above promises the split "has to survive" degenerate input and this chosen survival trades a zero-width column for an out-of-bounds row. Clamp the column count to what actually fits — the largest n with `spacing*(n-1) + n <= availableSize`, i.e. `((availableSize + spacing) / (spacing + 1)).coerceAtLeast(1)` (assumes `spacing >= 0`) — instead of only flooring the widths.

comments.content: The count is decided with `gridColumnCount`'s default `spacingDp = CardGridSpec.GridSpacing` (10.dp) while the widths below are cut with the grid's real `spacing` in px — sized for one gap, split with another. All five converted screens use `Arrangement.spacedBy(10.dp)` (verified), so today's geometry holds, but the coupling is silent: a future grid with `spacedBy(16.dp)` gets a count computed for 10.dp and widths cut for 16.dp, which can push a column past the 550.dp cap and reflow the approved layout with no warning. (Deriving `spacingDp = spacing / density` is not a drop-in fix — at densities where 10.dp rounds to a non-whole px it would shift counts and break the pinned geometry.) Consider making the invariant unbreakable: have `CardGridSpec` own the spacing and export the `Arrangement`/`Dp` that the grids consume, so the gap and the count cannot drift apart.

comments.content: Correctness of the reconstruction depends entirely on convention: `contentPaddingHorizontal` must equal, per side, the number the grid writes into its `contentPadding`, or the count drifts — the hard "visuals already approved" constraint of this PR. I verified all five call sites are currently in sync (AppsRoot 12↔start/end 12.dp, FeedRoot 12↔12, HomeRoot 12↔12, CategoryListRoot 12↔horizontal 12, SearchRoot's default 0.dp↔its zero horizontal padding), but a single edited literal will silently change the column count. Consider single-sourcing the pair — e.g. a factory that returns the cells *and* the matching `PaddingValues`, or one that accepts a `PaddingValues` and extracts the horizontal inset — so a call site cannot hand the grid and the cells different numbers. Also, the class doc's "keep the declaration inside the container … so what is measured here is what the grid measures" does not apply to these implementations: `availableSize` arrives from the grid at layout time, the declaration site changes nothing, and only the parameter value has to track the grid's `contentPadding`.

comments.content: `spacingDp` is the one input the guards above skip, and `coerceAtLeast` is a no-op for NaN (all NaN comparisons are false): with NaN spacing `denom` stays NaN, `raw` becomes `NaN.toInt() = 0`, and the count lands on 1 via `coerceIn` — bounded, but by accident of the outer clamp rather than the documented degenerate-input path, while `MIN_POSITIVE`'s claim that it "guards … when the spacing is misconfigured" quietly does not hold (±Infinity spacing also collapses to NaN math). Today's callers only pass literals, so there is no live defect; for consistency fold `spacingDp` into the same `isFinite()` guard.

comments.content: `LazyGridLayoutInfo` has no `maxSpan` property (its API surface is `visibleItemsInfo`, `viewportStartOffset/EndOffset`, `totalItemsCount`, `viewportSize`, `beforeContentPadding/afterContentPadding`, `mainAxisItemSpacing`), and no project extension defines one — a repo-wide search finds `maxSpan` only on this line. The lane count is `maxLineSpan`, which is only exposed inside `LazyGridItemSpanScope` (the `span = { GridItemSpan(maxLineSpan) }` lambdas used in AppsRoot.kt), so this is an unresolved reference and will not compile. Even if a `maxSpan` existed on the info object, it would name the grid's max item span, not the line's cell count as the comment claims — conflating the two is what the next issue is about. Fix: pass the column count into `GridScrollbarAdapter` (the call sites' `WidthCappedGridCells`/`GridCells.Fixed` already know it) or derive it from visible spans and accept the window bias.

1. **`layoutInfo.maxSpan` (jvm:248) and `item.span` (jvm:256)** — The project uses `GridItemSpan(maxLineSpan)` (AppsRoot), i.e., the Compose span API where spans are `GridItemSpan`/`LazyGridItemSpanInfo` value classes and the lane count is `maxLineSpan` from `LazyGridItemSpanScope` — NOT `LazyGridLayoutInfo.maxSpan` (which doesn't exist on `LazyGridLayoutInfo`) and not a numeric `LazyGridItemInfo.span`. So `maxOf(layoutInfo.maxSpan, 1)` is an unresolved reference and `lineSpanSum += item.span` would be `Long.plus(GridItemSpan)` — build break. High severity (critical-ish; I'll use "high" per plan).

2. **Estimator dimension mixup (jvm:268)** — `avgLineHeight = heightSum / visibleItems.size` is px-per-item, multiplied by `estimatedLines` (a line count). Dimensions only balance when every item has the same span. AppsRoot's grid — the sole consumer of `GridScrollbarAdapter` — mixes 6 full-line items with normal cards (confirmed at AppsRoot 355/365/374/489/609/700). For a window with 1 full-line banner of height H and 3 cards of height h per 2 lines, the formula over/under-estimates by factor (H+3h)/(2(H+h)). Fix: weight each item's height by its line share: `weightedHeightSum += item.size.height * span / lanes`, `avgLineHeight = weightedHeightSum / linesOccupied` — exact for both uniform and mixed spans. High.

3. **Window-mix extrapolation bias (jvm:262-263)** — `linesPerItem = linesOccupied / visibleItems.size` extrapolates the visible window's span mix over the whole list. AppsRoot spreads full-line headers/banners through the list (import banner at top, "header-pending-installs", "updates-banner", "header-up-to-date", trailing spacer at end) — a window containing a full-line item has different `linesPerItem` and `avgLineHeight` than a window of only cards, so the estimated content size (→ thumb size and drag target) jumps as the user scrolls past each header. comments.content: Both statistics are extrapolated from whatever items happen to be in the visible window (`linesPerItem = linesOccupied / visibleItems.size`, `avgLineHeight = heightSum / visibleItems.size`), which assumes the span/height mix is uniform across the list. It isn't: Apps spreads full-line items through the list (import banner at top, `header-pending-installs`, `updates-banner`, `header-up-to-date`, `trailing-spacer` at the end). A window containing a header produces a different `linesPerItem` and `avgLineHeight` than a window of only cards, so the estimated content size — and with it the thumb size and every drag target — jumps as the user scrolls each header into or out of the window. That is thumb jitter on the exact screens this PR targets. Consider computing the per-item scale from the dominant (1-span) items and letting full-line items contribute only their own line, or otherwise damping the estimate so it does not swing with the window's mix.

comments.content: Scroll-state lifecycle: `rememberLazyGridState()` lives inside the `else ->` branch of this `when`. Every time the branch is left and re-entered — e.g. a search query filters `filteredApps` to empty (the `state.filteredApps.isEmpty()` branch) and is then cleared, or `state.isLoading` briefly flips true — the remembered grid state is discarded and recreated, so the scroll position is silently lost and the grid visibly re-anchors. Hoist `listState` (and `rememberWidthCappedGridCells`, which is also branch-scoped below) to `AppsScreen` scope so their lifetime spans all `when` branches. (The scoping predates this PR — the old `rememberLazyListState()` sat here too — but this migration is the right moment to fix it.)

comments.content: The comment misdescribes what this assertion guards. `assertEquals(16, …)` is reached only because `coerceAtLeast(MIN_POSITIVE)` forces the denominator to `0.001`, yielding `ceil(1400/0.001) ≈ 1.4e6`, which `coerceIn(1, MAX_COLUMNS)` then clamps to 16. A regression that *stopped* the `coerceAtLeast` input clamp would compute `denom = 270 + (-1000) = -730`, so `raw = ceil(1400/-730) = -1` and `coerceIn(1,16)` lands on **1** — it would NOT "sail past 16". The "sail past 16" outcome is what you get from removing the *output* `coerceIn` clamp (with the input clamp still present → 1.4e6). As written, the phrase "a clamped-input regression that stopped clamping would sail past 16" conflates the two clamps and points at the wrong one. The value 16 is correct and does catch both regressions, but the rationale should distinguish them so a maintainer doesn't "fix" the wrong guard.
